h: Canals, Cocktails and a Cracking Location
p: The Cube is one of Birmingham's more striking buildings, a big, patterned block standing by the canal near the Mailbox. That puts you in one of the nicest parts of the city for a stroll, especially as the evening lights start reflecting off the water.

Before your lane booking, take a walk along the towpath to Gas Street Basin, where narrowboats line up at what was once the hub of Birmingham's canal network. It's said the city has more miles of canal than Venice, a claim locals love to throw at visitors. Brindleyplace is just along the water, with plenty of bars and restaurants, and the Library of Birmingham, with its distinctive metal-ringed exterior, is a short walk away on Centenary Square.
The Mailbox itself has shops and places to eat, so it's handy if half the group arrives early and needs somewhere to wait. New Street station is a short walk for anyone coming in by train.

Group tips for a smooth night: book well ahead for Fridays and Saturdays, and arrive a little early to get shoes and drinks sorted. Agree teams before you start so nobody's still faffing after the first frame. If the group includes complete beginners, put one confident bowler in each team to keep it even. And for a really competitive crowd, decide the stakes beforehand, whether that's buying the round, picking the karaoke song or carrying everyone's coats home. Sorted.
